<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212` — the merge of head `36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8` into base `e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212 && git checkout ef691dd87ec57f7eba1edd4b36bc4f714a24c212
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42 && git merge --no-ff 36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e8a78c4bdf0ec079cdb56e6e6c6f32d6f4ac8e42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L2 round on head 60d4e1c6c7: finding S1 sent back · 2026-11-17T22:46Z

The seat's at-tier reviewer sub-agent read this head and found no must-fix, one should-fix, and three nits. Its record is NOT posted as the record of this head: `verify-review-tier.mjs` refused its transcript, because one turn is a synthetic usage-limit error turn (every model turn is CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER). The rule is a fresh at-tier run, never a renamed tier. S1 moves the head anyway, so the fresh record is rendered on the fixed head.

**S1 (should-fix).** The record-root date-text pass stands down on any operator fault of the roots' Timestamp typing (`recordRootReadsFaultTimestampTyping` matches `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE`), not only on the date-arith shape it defers to. So, read from the tree and the cel-js 8.0.0 checker (not run):
- (a) `record.due_date - record.borrow_date GT 3` gives 0 findings, while the bare spelling is refused (`date-text-arithmetic-run-fails`, the registered `formula-date-subtraction-refused` shape).
- (b) `record.due_date GE "2026-01-01" && timestamp(record.borrow_date) LT now()` gives 0 findings, but is refused with the conjuncts swapped, so the answer depends on operand order. The bare spelling is refused in both orders.
Fix sent to the dev: route (i), stand down only where the roots' Timestamp-typing fault is date-arith. Pin (a), and (b) in both orders, and keep the `record.due_date + 1` control.

Nits sent along: N1, one shared constant for the root-read gate (`RECORD_ROOT_READ_RE`) and `firstTypeMismatch`'s inline one. N2, `firstTypeMismatch`'s comment "The date verdicts stay the bare name's alone" is now true of date-arith only. N3, a `-run-may-fail` root-read pin at the lint or door layer is optional.
Also noted by the reviewer, for a follow-up card: the index spelling `timestamp(record['borrow_date'])` reaches neither pass.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `36a9089a809745c2a0e02ee245a643ae73db07c8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, .changeset/34662-flow-record-date-text.md, packages/formula/src/validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-flow-condition-record-date-text.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-schema-e2e.test.ts + packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-subtraction-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-date-text-call-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.formula-timestamp-date-only-refused.ts, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md
Security-touching: no

PR #34935 (card #34662), face `narrowing`: `reviewFace` returns no `hits` on this file list, so the floor is the diff itself. ④ grades the two implementing files and the changeset's declaration text; the four test files were read as the pins of those sentences and stay the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT (6997857940). The files after `+` are outside the diff: read to judge, not reviewed. Inputs: the card body and all eight card comments, the PR body, file list and comments, the net diff `origin/main...36a9089a80` (merge base `e8a78c4bdf`, seven files, +583 −27), the merged blobs of `validate.ts` and `cel-engine.ts` at the head, and the 68 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run; every "gives N findings" below that is not a CI-pinned case is read off the tree and says so.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Flow condition accept-set (start, edge, `decision` branch), `os validate` / `os build`: narrowed. Right.** `typeSoundnessIssue` now returns `bare ?? recordRootDateTextIssue(...)` at flattened scope only (validate.ts:556). In `@objectstack/lint` the only `check(...)` calls that reach the flattened default with an `objectName` (hence `fieldTypes`) are the three flow sites (validate-expressions.ts:3097, 3511, 3749); `app landing visible` (4653) hands no object. So "in a flow condition" in the changeset is the true extent in lint.
- **Flow publish door (`publishMetaItem`): narrowed to `INVALID_METADATA` / 422. Right**, through the shared pass; pinned in the new runtime test, item left `draft`.
- **`registerFlow`: accept-set unchanged, advisory text gains the root read. Right.** flow-registration-checks.ts:745 hands the flattened hint with `fieldTypes` and no `faultOutcome`, so the arm there is `run-may-fail`; registration stays additive (#1928).
- **MCP expression tool, kind `flow_condition`: its answer narrows the same way. Right, and not named in the changeset.** mcp-http-tools.ts:2693 declares the kind at `scope: 'flattened'` and hands `fieldTypes` (3577 to 3607), so the tool now answers the refusal the gate gives. That is the tool's contract ("answers what the gate will"); the changeset's "Where" bullet omits it (N6).
- **Record-scoped sites and the flow value envelope: unchanged. Right.** `firstDateTextVerdict` and `firstDateTextCall` drop `recordRootTypes` unless `scope === 'flattened'`; `flowValueEnvelopeDateTextIssue` passes none.
- **Refusals only where nothing was reported before. Right.** The root pass runs only when `firstTypeMismatch` answered null and the bare date-text pass answered null, and keeps only `date-text-call*` / `date-text-arithmetic*`. No existing verdict changes code, grade or words.
- **Verdict surface: no new code, no new param key. Right.** `reference`, `call`, `rewrite`, `shift` carry the read as written (`record.borrow_date`); the arm is `dateArm('flattened', faultOutcome, false)`, the #30025 precedent for a root read.
- **Package public surface: nothing added. Right.** `packages/formula/src/index.ts` at the head re-exports neither `RECORD_ROOT_READ_RE`, `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith`, `firstDateTextVerdict`, `firstDateTextCall` nor `DateTextVerdict`; the package has one export path (`.`). The new `export` keywords are module-level only.
- **Run-time evaluator: unchanged. Right.** No hunk outside the check-only paths.
- **Typed-env cache (main's #34756 / PR #35000, auto-merged): the key covers every input. Right.** `buildTypedEnv` keys on `JSON.stringify([scope, temporal, fieldCelTypes, recordRootTypes ?? null])` (cel-engine.ts:1108) and `createTypedEnv` reads exactly those four plus module constants. The three shapes this PR asks for are distinct keys: `({}, flattened, timestamp, roots)` for the stand-down probe, `({}, flattened, date-text, roots)` and `({}, flattened, text, textTyping(roots))` for the root pass; `{}` with roots never collides with roots as the bare map and `null`. `dateOnlyFields` is not an env input (read after the check), so it rightly is not in the key. No code in this diff registers on a returned env: all three callers only `parse` and `check`, the condition the cache's docblock sets.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34662-flow-record-date-text.md`: `'@objectstack/formula': minor`, `fix(formula)!:` heading, **BREAKING** banner, FROM-to-TO table, line-leading `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, identical in the PR body. Matches what the diff publishes: a refusal where a publish was admitted, and no widening (① public surface). `minor` is the level the repo gives a `narrowed` change; `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success` on this head. The only source change is in `@objectstack/formula`; lint, runtime, service-automation and mcp change by dependency alone and carry test files only, so one package in the changeset is right.

ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (already-registered ...)`: the three ids exist under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/`, and each `surface` already names flow conditions and the `record` (or `previous`) read. No entry moved. `Skills-docs: none` holds: SKILL.md:164 to 166 states the `date-text-call` rule with `record.FIELD` spellings and no site limit.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_question 1 (which declaration lines stand):** answered by the seat's revised claim 6955917834, `no (narrowing)` / `narrowed`. Agreed, on ① and ②.
- **open_question 2 (`registerFlow` named as the door):** answered there too, accepted as landed. Agreed: `publishMetaItem` refuses, `registerFlow` advises, and it does not refuse the bare name either.
- **Dev flag, `record.due_date + 1` passes while the bare name is refused (`date-arithmetic` family):** filed as #34946 (card comment 6958215971). The stand-down in this PR is what keeps that shape for that card. Answered.
- **Dev flag, a flow variable named `record` is still typed as the row:** accepted deviation; the `type-mismatch` root pass has the same behaviour and this diff does not alter it.
- **Earlier reviewer's note, the index spelling `timestamp(record['borrow_date'])` reaches neither pass:** the seat's hold comment 6963236571 and the dev report say "the seat files it"; no card number appears in the inputs I was given. Escalated to the seat: name the card, or file it together with N5 below.
- **Dev deviation, local suite and typecheck NOT MEASURED at the merge head:** the check-runs are the verdict here. On `36a9089a80`: 57 `success`, 11 `skipped`, none failed; `Test Core` and its ten shards, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):** not applicable. No hunk reads data, materialises ids or joins; the diff is a type check over expression source.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Earlier graded findings (round on `60d4e1c6c7`, comment 6963236571), state on this head:

- S1: closed. `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith` (cel-engine.ts:1601) returns true only when the roots' first Timestamp-typing fault matches `isDateArith`; the merge left it intact. Both S1 shapes are pinned in the formula harness (root and bare, (b) in both orders) and `Test Core` is green on this head.
- N1: closed. One `RECORD_ROOT_READ_RE` (cel-engine.ts:1264) gates `firstTypeMismatch`'s root pass and `recordRootDateTextIssue`.
- N2: closed. The `firstTypeMismatch` comment (1416 to 1421) now says the `date-arith` verdict alone stays the bare name's.
- N3: closed. The lint harness pins the `run-may-fail` sentence on an untriggered flow for the bare name and both roots.

**`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`** — agrees with the contract.

- *Order.* The docblock says the pass follows the bare name's own order. Read against the tree: for the bare name `firstTypeMismatch` answers `date-arith` when the first Timestamp-typing fault is date or duration arithmetic against a number, a text or boolean mismatch when the date-text re-check confirms it, and null otherwise; only null reaches the date-text check. The root pass is entered only on null (the type-mismatch root verdict already won at 534 to 548), and stands down on exactly the one remaining shape. Tried against it: `timestamp(record.borrow_date) LT now() && record.due_date + 1 GT 5` (the call faults the Timestamp typing first, not an operator fault, so it is judged, as the bare spelling is); the reverse order stands down, where the bare spelling gets `date-arithmetic`: the #34946 gap, not a new one. `record.due_date LT 5 && timestamp(record.borrow_date) LT now()` is judged on both spellings.
- *Typing.* Roots get every field's type and `dateOnly` is built from all fields, not the shadow-filtered set: right, a flow variable shadows a bare name and never a root member (pinned). Bare names are passed as `{}`, so the root pass can only fault on a root read and can never attach the row's arm to a bare-name fault.
- *Arm.* `dateArm('flattened', faultOutcome, false)`: `run-fails` only where the producer declared it, else `run-may-fail`; the grade is `error` on both, as for the bare name. An untriggered flow whose caller hands a full instant under `record.borrow_date` is refused although it would run; the bare name has had that grade since #30016, so this is parity, not a new false refusal.
- *Filter.* `DATE_TEXT_FAMILY_RE` drops `date-duration-value`, which a flattened `value` role could otherwise surface through the root pass. Right.
- *False refusals looked for and not found:* `datetime` under `timestamp()` (not in `dateOnly`; pinned CONTROL at four layers), `date(record.FIELD)` (pinned, evaluates true), `input.FIELD` (`typingOf` answers `undefined` for any root but `record` / `previous` on this pass; pinned), ordering against a text literal or a Timestamp and `today() - record.FIELD` in a predicate (declared date-text overloads, check clean).

**`packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`** — agrees with the contract.
